variant.stem_override: A 35-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus has been in clinical remission on hydroxychloroquine 400 mg/d and low-dose prednisone 5 mg/d for the past 12 months (SLEDAI-2K consistently 0–2). She has no history of lupus nephritis. Routine serologic monitoring at her current visit shows anti-dsDNA antibody 340 IU/mL (rising from 80 over the past 4 months), C3 62 mg/dL (declining from 95 over the same period), and C4 8 mg/dL (declining from 18). She is CLINICALLY asymptomatic — no fatigue, no rash, no arthritis. Today's urinalysis is bland (no proteinuria, no casts, no hematuria); CBC, creatinine, and liver enzymes are normal. She reports well-controlled seasonal allergic rhinitis managed with as-needed cetirizine. There has been no change in her medications or lifestyle.
variant.rationale_for_variant: A single incidental fact — well-controlled seasonal allergic rhinitis on as-needed cetirizine — was inserted as a distractor. It is unrelated to SLE serologic activity and supports no answer option; the picture of serologically active, clinically quiescent SLE is unchanged, so the correct answer (A) stands.
